Soil Quality and Fertilizers Sectional Committee, FAD 07 


FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Soil Quality 
and Fertilizers Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council 


Bio fertilizers have been identified as alternative to chemical fertilizers to increase soil fertility and crop production 
in sustainable farming. Bio fertilizers are natural fertilizers which are microbial inoculants of bacteria, algae, fungi 
alone, or in combination, and they augment the availability of nutrients to the plants. The use of bio fertilizers, 
in preference to chemical fertilizers, offers economic and ecological benefits by way of soil health and fertility to 
farmers. 


Biofertilizers are products containing living cells of different types of microorganisms, which have the ability to 
convert nutritionally important elements from unavailable to available form through biological processes. They 
are involved in symbiotic and associative microbial activities with higher plants. These are natural mini-fertilizer 
factories that are economical and safer source of plant nutrition for increasing the agricultural production and 
improving soil fertility. 

Since the development and commercialization of phosphate solubilizing bacterial and fungal inoculants, 
voluminous data has been generated on the synergistic effects of these micro-organisms when they are applied 
together. Now it has been established beyond doubt that combined application of nitrogen fixing, phosphate 
solubilizing and growth promoting bacteria delivers best results. Since last many years, combined application of 
at least one nitrogen fixing and phosphate solubilizing bacteria is being promoted and recommended. Keeping 
in view the advantages of combined application, various industries have developed their own mixed inoculants 
combining either two (one N-fixer + PSBI), three (one N-fixer + PSBI + KMBI) or four bio fertilizer organisms 
(one or two N-fixer + PSBI + KMBI + Pseudomonas fluorescens). 


The Consortia of Microbial Inoculants (CMI) include different groups of beneficial soil micro-organisms, such 
as nitrogen fixers, phosphate solubilizers, potash mobilizers, zinc solubilizers and plant growth promoters which 
harvest the nutrients in unavailable form from the air and soil and convert them into plant usable form. Some bacteria 
secrete growth promoting hormones and help in plant growth and root development through their hormonal action. 
The species of Rhizobium, Azotobacter, Azospirillum, Bacillus, Pseudomonas, Fraturia, Gluconacetobacter, 
Pseudomonas fluorescens etc. are active in such bioconversion. These efficient micro-organisms have shown 
capability to mobilize nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium and zinc content available in the soil as natural reserve or 
supplied through fertilizer application in the soil. 


Many brands of CMI are marketed in the country and they have been found to vary in quality. Hence, the need was 
felt for an Indian Standard not only to test the quality of inoculants in order to provide the farmers with certified 
inoculants but also to help the producers to improve quality of their products. 


The composition of the Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given at Annex E. 


It is obligatory on the part of the manufacturers to employ qualified soil microbiologist or microbiologist or 
agricultural graduates or graduates in biology trained in soil microbiology in their staff. Manufacturers shall also 
maintain a quality control laboratory capable of carrying out the tests according to this standard. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 1960 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )’. The number of significant places retained in the 
rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 17755 : 2022 


Indian Standard 


CONSORTIA OF MICROBIAL INOCULANTS 
(MIXED BIOFERTILIZER INOCULANTS ) — 
SPECIFICATION 


1 SCOPE 


The standard prescribes the requirements, method 
of sampling and tests for Consortia of Microbial 
Inoculants (CMI). 


2 REFERENCE 


The following Indian Standards contain provisions 
which through reference in this text constitutes 
provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, 
the editions indicated were valid. All standards are 
subject to revision, and parties to agreements based 
on this standard are encouraged to investigate the 
possibility of applying the most recent edition of the 
standard indicated below: 


IS No. Title 
460 (Part 1): Test sieves— Specification 
2020 Part 1 Wire cloth test sieves 

(fourth revision) 

1070 : 1992 Reagent grade water (third revision) 

6850: 1973 Specification for agar, 
microbiological grade 

6853: 1973 Specification for peptone, 
microbiological grade 

7004:1973 Specification for yeast extract, 
microbiological grade 

8268: 2020 Rhizobium inoculants — 
Specification (third revision) 

9138 : 2020 Azotobacter Spp. Inoculants —- 
Specification (third revision) 

14806 : 2000 Azospirillum inoculants 

14807 : 2021 Phosphate solubilising bacterial 
inoculant (PSBI) — Specification 
(first revision) 

17672 : 2021 Potash Mobilizing Bacterial 
Inoculant (KMBI) — Specification 

3 TERMINOLOGY 


For the purpose of this standard, the following 
definitions shall apply. 


3.1.1 Consortia of Microbial Inoculants (CMI) 


CMl is a product having high population of two or more 
beneficial plant growth promoting microorganisms and 
their strain(s) intended to improve plant growth and 
productivity through the processes of nitrogen fixation, 
nutrient solubilization or mobilization and through 
plant growth promotion. 


3.1.2 Group of Crops 


CMIs can be crop specific or of wide spectrum in nature 
for use in all types of crops for nutrient mobilization 
and growth promotion. 


4 REQUIREMENTS 


4.1 CMI shall be carrier based, colour depending on the 
colour of carrier. Carrier material, such as peat, lignite, 
charcoal or similar material may be used. In case carrier 
is acidic in nature, then it shall be neutralized with 
calcium carbonate and then sterilized. When tested for 
fineness, it shall pass through 0.15-0.212 mm IS sieve 
[(see IS 460 (Part 1)]. 


4.2 When tested by the method prescribed in Annex A of 
this standard, CMI shall contain a minimum of | x 10° 
viable cells of each of the constituent microorganism 
individually, per gram of the carrier material on dry 
mass basis during the entire period of shelf life, as 
specified on the packet. 


4.3 When tested by the method prescribed in Annex 
A, CMI shall have no contamination with other 
micro-organisms at 10° dilution. 


4.4 When tested by the method prescribed in Annex B 
of IS 8268, the pH of CMI shall be 5.0 to 7.5. 


4.5 Individual microorganism present in CMI as per 
label claim, shall demonstrate minimum bio efficacy 
value as follows: 


Rhizobium effective nodulation on all 
the legume species listed 
on the pack 

Azotobacter 10 mg N fixation/g of 
C-source utilized 

Azospirillum 10 mg of N-fixation/g of 


malate applied 


IS 17755 : 2022 


Phosphate Solubilizing 10 mm zone of 


Bacterial Inoculant solubilization on PSBI 

(PSBI) — Specification media having at least 

(first Revision) 3 mm thickness 

Potash Mobilizing 10 mm zone of 

Bacterial Inoculant solubilization on KMBI 

(KMBI)— Specification media having at least 
3 mm thickness 

Zinc Solubilizing 10 mm zone of 


solubilization on ZnSBI 
media having at least 
3 mm thickness 


Bacterial Inoculant 
(ZnSBI) Specification 


Pseudomonas Indole positive reaction as 
per the method prescribed 
in Annex B 

fluorescens 


The bio efficacy value for Rhizobium inoculants shall 
be tested as described in IS 8268; for Azotobacter as 
per IS 9138 and Azospirillum as per IS 14806, for PSBI 
as per IS 14807; for KMBI as per IS 17672 and for 
Pseudomonas fluorescens as per method prescribed in 
Annex B of this standard. 


4.6 Specified mother culture shall be obtained from any 
recognized institution maintaining the mother culture. 
The manufacturer may control the quality of broth as 
given in Annex C, and get it verified at least by two 
institutions as mentioned below. 
NOTE — At present National Centre of Organic Farming 
(NCOF), Ghaziabad and its six Regional Centres located 
at Bangalore, Bhubaneshwar, Hissar, Imphal, Jabalpur and 
Nagpur; Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI), 
New Delhi; Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU), 
Coimbatore; University of Agricultural Science, Bengaluru are 
sources for supplying the mother culture. 


5 PACKING, MARKING AND STORAGE 


5.1 Packing 


CMI shall be packed in packaging material of low 
density polyethylene or polypropylene bags thickness 
of which shall not be less than 75 micron or in suitable 
HDPE or polypropylene or plastic or glass bottles. 


5.2 Marking 
5.2.1 The following particulars shall be legibly and 
indelibly marked on package: 


a) Name of the product specially as ‘CONSORTIA 
OF MICROBIAL INOCULANT?’; 


b) Name and address of the manufacturer; 


c) Crop(s) for which intended; 

d) Type of the carrier; 

e) Batch number; 

f) Date of manufacture; 

g) Expiry date which shall not be less than 6 months 
from the date of manufacture: 

h) Net quantity in kg and area meant for; 


j) Storage instructions worded as under “STORE 
IN COOL PLACE AWAY FROM DIRECT 
SUNLIGHT AND HEAT”; and 


k) Any other information required under the Legal 
Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011. 


5.2.2 Items (c), (f) and (g) shall be printed on a coloured 
ink background. 


5.2.3 Directions for use of CMI shall be printed briefly 
on the packets as given in Annex D of this standard. A 
separate pamphlet may preferably be given with it. 


5.2.4 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of 
this standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules 
and Regulations framed thereunder, and the products 
may be marked with the Standard Mark. 


5.3 Storage 


CMI shall be stored by the manufacturer in a cool 
and dry place away from direct heat preferably at a 
temperature of 20 °C and not exceeding 30 °C. It shall 
also be the duty of the manufacturer to instruct the 
retailers and, in turn, the users about the precautions to 
be taken during storage. 


6 SAMPLING 


The representative samples of the CMI shall be drawn 
as prescribed in Annex F of IS 8268. 


7 TESTS 


7.1 Tests shall be carried out by the methods prescribed 
in 4. 


7.2 Unless otherwise specified, quality reagents, 
chemicals and distilled water (see IS 1070) shall be 
employed in tests. 


NOTE — ‘Pure chemicals’ shall mean chemicals that do not 
contain impurities which affect experimental results. 


IS 17755 : 2022 


ANNEX A 
( Clause 4.2 and 4.3 ) 
DETERMINATION OF NUMBER OF INDIVIDUAL MICROBIAL CELLS 


A-1 APPARATUS 

A-1.1 Pipettes, graduated, 1 ml and 10 ml. 
A- 1.2 Conical Flasks, 150 ml and 250 ml. 
A- 1.3 Screw Capped Tubes, 10 ml. 
A-1.4 Incubator 

A-1.5 Petri Dishes 

A-1.6 Hot Air Oven 

A-1.7 Autoclave 

A-1.8 pH Meter 

A-2 REAGENTS 


A-2.1 Use a medium of following compositions for 
different microorganisms: 


A-2.1.1 Medium for Enumeration of Rhizobium 


Agar (see 6850) 20g 
Yeast extract (see 7004) lg 
Mannitol 10g 
Potassium hydrogen phosphate (K,HPO,) 0.5 g 
Magnesium sulphate (MgSO,.7H,O) 0.2 g 
Sodium chloride (NaCl) 0.1 g 
Congo red 2.5 ml 
Distilled water 1 000 ml 
pH 7.0 


A-2.1.2 Medium for Enumeration of Azotobacter 


Agar 20g 
Sucrose (C,,H,,O,,) 20g 
Ferric sulphate Fe,(SO,), 0.1 g 
Dibasic potassium phosphate (K,HPO,) 1.0g 
Magnesium sulphate (MgSO, 7H,O) 0.5g 
Sodium chloride (NaCl) 0.5 g 
Calcium carbonate (CaCO,) 2.0 g 
Sodium molybdate (Na,MoO,) 0.005 g 
Distilled water 1 000 ml 
pH 6.8 to 7.2 


A-2.1.3 Medium for Enumeration of Azospirillum 
(Nitrogen Free Bromothymol Blue Medium) 


Malic acid 5.0 g 
Potassium hydroxide 4.0g 
Di-potassium hydrogen phosphate 0.5g 
Ferrous sulphate 0.05 g 
Manganese sulphate 0.01 g 
Magnasium sulphate 0.1 g 
Sodium chloride 0.2 ¢ 
Calcium chloride Olg 
Sodium molybdate 0.002 g 
Distilled water 1 000 ml 
Bromothymol blue 2.0 ml 
(0.5 Percent alcoholic solution) 

Agar 1.7g 
pH adjusted to 6.5 - 7.0 


NOTE — Colour of the medium should be pale green. 


A-2.1.4 Medium for Enumeration of Phosphate 
Solubilizing Microorganisms 


Glucose 10.0 g 
Tri-calcium phosphate 5.0 g 
Ammonium sulphate 0.5g 
Magnesium sulphate olg 
Sodium chloride 0.2g 
Yeast extract 0.5g 
Manganese sulphate Trace 
Ferrous sulphate Trace 
Distilled water 1 000 ml 
Agar 15.0 g 
pH adjusted to + 0.2 


A-2.1.5 Medium for Enumeration of Potassium 
Mobilizing Microorganisms (Aleksandrov Medium) 


Glucose 5g 
Magnesium sulphate 0.005g 
Ferric chloride 0.lg 
Calcium carbonate 2.0g 


IS 17755 : 2022 


Potassium alumino silicate (mica powder) 2.0g 
Calcium phosphate 2.0g 
Distilled water 1 000 ml 


Mix all the ingredients in about 750 ml of water, 
except glucose and autoclave. Filter sterilized glucose 
dissolved in 250 ml water is mixed with above solution 
after autoclaving. 


A-2.1.6 Medium for Enumeration of Zinc Solubilizing 
Microorganisms 


Glucose 10g 
Zinc oxide 1.0g 
Ammonium sulphate 0.5g 
Potassium chloride 0.2g 
Yeast extract 0.5g 
Ferrous sulphate 0.01 g 
Manganese sulphate 0.01 g 
Dipotassium hydrogen phosphate 0.5g 
Distilled water 1 000 ml 


A-2.1.7 Medium for Enumeration of Pseudomonas 
Fluorescens (Kings B Medium) 


Proteose peptone (see 6853) 20g 


Glycerol 10g 


K,HPO, 1.5g 
MgS0,.7H,O 1.5g 
Agar 15g 
Distilled water 1 000 ml 
pH adjusted to 7:2 


A-2.3 Sterilization and preparation process for plates is 
the same as described in IS 8268. 


A-3 PREPARATION OF SERIAL DILUTION 
FOR CELL COUNT METHOD 


Dispense 30 g of CMI in 270 ml of sterile water and 
shake for 10 minutes on a reciprocal shaker. Make 
serial dilutions up to 107 level. Pipette out 0.2 ml 
aliquots of 10° to 10’ dilution and deliver it on the petri 
dishes containing set medium as described in A-2.1 
on respective medium of each microorganisms to be 
enumerated, except Azospirillum. Spread the aliquots 
over the plate. Invert the plates and place them in the 
incubator at 28 + 2 °C for 7 days. Use 3 replicates of 
10°, 10° and 107 dilution. For Azospirillum, use the 
methods as described in IS 14806. 


A-4 COUNTING 


Count total number of colonies on the plates/tubes as 
per the method described for each microorganism. 


IS 17755 : 2022 


ANNEX B 
( Clause 4.5 ) 


METHODS FOR ENUMERATION OF BIOEFFICACY CHARACTERISTICS OF 
PSEUDOMONAS FLUORESCENS 


B-1 METHOD FOR INDOLE REACTION 
ASSAY 


B-1-1 Medium for Growing Bacteria 


Add 0.25 g of Tryptophan into 1 litre of Kings B 
medium as given in A-2.1.7. 


B-1.2 Growing Bacteria in Specified Medium 


Fill 125 ml medium in six conical flasks and autoclave 
at 121°C for 15 min. After cooling, inoculate 
3 flasks with loopful of bacteria (from a colony of 
Pseudomonas fluorescens grown on Kings B medium) 
and incubate for 5 days under continuous shaking at 
28+2°C. Keep 3 unioculated flasks as control. After 
5 days of incubation, centrifuge the broth at 15 000 rpm 
for 30 min and collect the supernatant. Use this clear 
centrifuged solution for indole reaction. 


B-1.3 Reagents 
B-1.3.1 Stock Solution of 0.5M Ferric Chloride (FeCl,) 


B-1.3.2 Stock Solution of 35 Percent Perchloric Acid 
(HCIO ) 


B-1.3.3 Orthophosphoric Acid 
B-1.4 Procedure 


B-1.4.1 Preparation of Salkowski Reagent — Suspend 
1 ml of 0.5M FeCl, in 50 ml of HCIO, (prepare fresh 
every time). 


B-1.4.2 Take 2 ml of centrifuged broth in a test tube, 
add 2-3 drops of orthophosphoric acid followed by 4 ml 
of freshly prepared Salkowski reagent. 


B-1.4.3 Incubate the tubes at room temperature for 
25 min and observe the colour. Development of pink 
colour in cultured broth is indicative of indole positive 
reaction. Uninoculated broth (control) shall show no 
colour development. 


ANNEX C 
( Clause 4.6 ) 


GUIDELINES ON MAINTENANCE AND PREPERATION OF CULTURE 
AND QUALITY CONTROL AT BROTH STAGE 


C-1 MAINTENANCE OF PURE CULTURES 


C-1.1 Maintain pure cultures of CMI on the medium as 
described in A-2.1 in the form of slants. 


C-1.2 Transfer a loopful of pure culture to each of 
the agar slants aseptically in an inoculation room and 
incubate at 28 + 2 °C for 7 days. Always keep pure 
culture below 5 °C. 


C-2 PREPARATION OF 
CULTURE AND MASS CULTURE 


INOCULUM 


Inoculum culture and mass culture shall be prepared 
as described in D-2 and D-3 of the IS 8268 changing 
the media composition as mentioned in A-2.1 of this 
standard. 


C-3 QUALITY CONTROL 
RECOMMENDED AT BROTH STAGE 


TEST 


C-3.1 Qualitative Test 


C-3.1.1 Check for freedom from visible contaminants 
by microscope and observing solubilization zones. 


C-3.1.2 pH of bacterial broth shall normally be between 
6.5 to 7. 


C-3.1.3 Gram staining test shall be carried out as 
described in D-4.1.3.1 and D-4.1.3.2 of IS 8268. 


C-3.2 Quantitative Test 


C-3.2.1 Viable Cell Count — As per the method 
mentioned at Annex A of this standard. 


IS 17755 : 2022 


ANNEX D 
( Clause 5.2.3 ) 


DIRECTION FOR USE OF CONSORTIA OF MICROBIAL INOCULANTS 


D-1 The contents of the packet are sufficient enough 
to the given quantity of seed for seed treatment or for 
given area to be broadcast or for given quantity of 
seedlings for root dipping depending on the specified 
crops as denoted on the packet. Mix the inoculants with 
seeds gently with the minimum amount of water, taking 
care to avoid damage to seed coat. Dry the inoculated 
seed under shade over clean dry paper or organic bag 
and sow immediately. For seedling treatment, suspend 
recommended quantity of inoculants in recommended 
quantity of water and keep the roots of seedlings dipped 


for 30-45 min immediately before transplanting. For 
soil treatment, mix recommended quantity of inoculants 
in 200-500 kg of mature compost and broadcast evenly 
over recommended area at the time of final ploughing 
before sowing. 


D-2 In order to get best benefits, use CMI in crops 
specified on the packet. Use before the expiry date and 
do not expose to direct sunlight or heat. 


D-3 CMI is not a chemical fertilizer, hence do not mix 
inoculated seeds or CMI with agro-chemicals.

Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis.in.
